2609.24965.title: Jev for Scientific Decisions: Evaluating Semantic Choices and Their Consequences
2609.24965.paper_summary: Scientific workflows often require choosing among known relations before a deterministic calculation can proceed. Whether observations share a culture, treatment or reference standard can change the scientific meaning of the resulting count or comparison. We evaluate Jev as a semantic decision component using a harness that follows its documented guidance and assigns arithmetic to code. The study compares twelve model configurations on twenty source-grounded Choices across ten scientific cases, each repeated five times. We measure semantic selections, downstream outputs and final claim labels separately. Jev matched five other configurations at complete semantic correctness and achieved the lowest observed median latency among successful responses. Across three comparison models, seven wrong selections on one culture-history question changed downstream counts while preserving the correct final label. These results identify a useful role for Jev in prepared scientific decision tasks and show why evaluating that role requires checking the relations and quantities that a workflow will reuse.
2609.24965.paper_summary_zh: 科學工作流程通常需要在已知關係中進行選擇，才能進行確定性計算。觀察是否共享文化、處理或參考標準，會改變結果計數或比較的科學意義。我們使用一個遵循其文檔指導並將算術分配給代碼的裝置，評估Jev作為語義決策組件。該研究在十個科學案例中，對二十個基於來源的選擇比較了十二個模型配置，每個配置重複五次。我們分別測量語義選擇、下游輸出和最終聲明標籤。Jev在完全語義正確性方面與其他五個配置相匹配，並在成功回應中實現了觀察到的最低中位延遲。在三個比較模型中，對一個文化歷史問題的七個錯誤選擇改變了下游計數，同時保留了正確的最終標籤。這些結果確定了Jev在準備的科學決策任務中的有用角色，並顯示出評估該角色為何需要檢查工作流程將重用的關係和數量。
